title: Email Manners
short: Write a clear subject, open with a greeting, keep it brief, proofread, reply within a day or two, and use "reply all" only when everyone needs it.
trouble: Learners write emails in all capitals, skip the greeting, or reply-all to a whole list with "thanks!" Email is permanent and easy to forward.

blocks.html: Email follows the same frame as a letter: a greeting, a body, a closing and your name. What changes is speed, which makes it easy to send something you will wish you had read again.
Write a clear subject, open with a greeting, keep it brief, proofread, and reply within a day or two. Use "reply all" only when everyone needs the reply.

A subject line lets busy people find your message and know what it is about before they open it. A greeting and a closing keep the tone friendly in a medium where tone is easy to misread. Short messages respect the reader's time. Email is permanent and easy to forward, so writing as if the whole office might read it is simply prudent. "Reply all" fills many inboxes at once, so it is for replies everyone truly needs.

parts.subject: Question about Thursday's meeting
parts.body: Could we move Thursday's meeting to 2 p.m.? I have a dentist appointment in the morning. I'm happy to send the report ahead so we can use the time well.

blocks.title: A better subject line
blocks.q: Hana's email to her professor is titled "Hi." What would be better?
steps: A subject should say what the email is about.
"Question about the essay due Friday" tells the professor at a glance.
blocks.a: A subject that names the topic.

blocks.title: Reply all?
blocks.q: Kofi's manager emails 40 people: "The office will close at 3 on Friday." Kofi wants to say thanks. Should he reply all?
steps: Forty people do not need to read his thanks.
If he wants to thank the manager, he replies only to her, or says nothing at all.
blocks.a: No. Reply only to the sender, if at all.

blocks.name: et-order

opts.title: Before you press Send
items: Say what you need in a few short lines
Proofread, and check who is on the To line

blocks.cap: Put the steps of an email in order.

blocks.html: Writing emails in all capitals, skipping the greeting, or replying all to a whole list with "thanks!" All capitals reads as shouting. Email is permanent and easy to forward; if you would not want it read aloud at a meeting, don't send it.
